title: Period, Symmetry, and Graph of s = sec(pi*t/2)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph the function s = \sec(\pi t / 2) in the ts-plane. Find the fundamental period of the function and state the symmetry of its graph.

steps.title: Compute the Fundamental Period
steps.explanation: Since secant shares the 2*pi period of cosine, dividing 2*pi by the angular frequency pi/2 gives a period of 4.

steps.title: Locate Vertical Asymptotes and Local Extrema
steps.explanation: Vertical asymptotes occur at odd integers t = +/-1, +/-3, ... where cos(pi*t/2) = 0. U-shaped branches open upward from (4k, 1) and downward from (4k + 2, -1).
steps.why: sec(theta) = 1/cos(theta) is undefined when cos(theta) = 0 and equals +/-1 when cos(theta) = +/-1.

steps.title: Determine Graph Symmetry
steps.explanation: Because cosine is an even function, its reciprocal secant is also even, so the graph is symmetric about the vertical axis (s-axis / y-axis).
steps.why: An even function satisfies s(-t) = s(t), reflecting the graph across the vertical axis onto itself.
